locators: p19 wire joining photographs and captions
supported_claims: The account describes measuring and cutting brass sheet into strips, shaping wavy edges with hammer and chisel, and curving body pieces into rings.
Successive rings are sized to fit within the preceding ring; pierced holes receive brass wire that ties components together.
The head is formed over a metal support; fins are cut from sheet. The p19 photographs show the overlapping body pieces and wire being inserted and secured.
limits: Do not copy a complete practical recipe or exact dimensions/ratios. Technical joining terminology is loose; avoid a categorical claim of no heat, no welding or no soldering anywhere in production.
Exclude ancient-origin/inventor claims, historic symbolism, wooden-fish replacement, current demand, prices and growing durability assertions.

Contact page has visibly inconsistent address 'Cuttack, Kerala / Orissa'; do not reproduce it or use its short name Pradip Maharana to assert identity with NIFT's named maker without further evidence.
Do not infer the photographed artisan's name from the contact listing alone.

sources.title: Craft Documentation of Flexible Brass Craft of Bellaguntha, Ganjam, Odisha, India
sources.author: Santosh Kumar Jha
sources.publisher: Chitrolekha International Magazine on Art and Design, vol.6 no.3, pp33–61; AesthetixMS
sources.access: Original PDF text read through web extraction. Coordinator downloaded original; researcher personally visually inspected complete printed pp33,44,55 (PDF pages1,12,23). Selected passages from pp34,54–57 read in extracted original text; not all 29 pages visually inspected.
locators: p57 section14 and Figure21 (text only in this review)
supported_claims: Jha's field account distinguishes relatively rigid head and tail parts from the articulated abdomen, composed of separately formed brass rings joined with wire.
The rings nest with clearance for movement; he describes shaping, checking their fit, piercing and wire-knotting. Figure18 shows several assembly stages.
The study names Pradeep Kumar Moharana and describes him teaching his son; this is evidence from the 2016 publication, not proof of today's workshop arrangements.
limits: Keep observational process descriptions separate from the paper's speculative antiquity/royal chronology and inherited origin narratives. Exclude origin dates, first inventor and family genealogy.
Exclude erroneous lead/radioactivity statement on p44 and ambiguous polishing chemical 'Sulfur Nitrate'; no chemical, lead-handling or construction advice.
Do not present 2016 counts, output, income, current demand or workshop address as current. Do not repeat 'only family', monopoly or extinction claims.
The anatomy labels and exact proportions are the author's chosen model, not a universal requirement. Not all products in the study have identical fins or shape.
